analyst_view.overall: Early view: Barcelona top the table with 48 goals in 12 games, but this comes four days after a Champions League trip to Sabah (25 November) and three days before hosting Atlético, and Flick keeps repeating that he has to 'look after the players', so rotation is likely. Promoted Deportivo go into the break on their first clean sheet (0-0 at Espanyol) but are without Eddahchouri after wrist surgery; Barça currently have Olmo, Rodri, Koundé and Bardghji out, and Lamine Yamal is being managed for right-knee discomfort.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.6 goals, driven by Barcelona scoring four a game. I lean a little lower: a rotated Barça between the Sabah trip and Atlético, against a Deportivo side that has conceded 14 in 12 and just shut out Espanyol, points to something nearer 3. Barça's own defence (13 conceded) also limits a Deportivo attack missing Eddahchouri.

corners.text: The numbers say 11 corners. Barcelona's recent games have been light on corners despite huge possession: 7 at Betis, 6 against Alavés and 6 at Atlético, with Barça themselves taking only 2-5 in three of their last four. Deportivo took 5 at Espanyol while sitting deep, so I lean lower, around 9.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards. Deportivo picked up four yellows defending at Espanyol and Amatucci is one booking from a ban, but Barça are rarely booked (one yellow at the Metropolitano). With no referee named yet, nothing moves me far from the number.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.2 shots. Barcelona have taken 13-19 shots in each of their last four league games and allowed 6-9, which adds up to the mid-20s rather than 28. Deportivo had only 5 shots at Espanyol with 36% of the ball, and a rotated Barça may control the game rather than chase volume.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 on target. Barça put only 4 of 19 shots on target at the Metropolitano, and Deportivo's attack is thin with Eddahchouri out and Yeremay coming back from gastroenteritis. I lean lower, around 8-9.
